title: PSG14C-S371 with a heralded filter: O(n^4 log n 2^(n/6)) work, O(n^2) bits, O(n) qubits, O(n^4) copies, tolerance 1-1/(10^64-3)^4

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N). Use the single PSG14C-S371 algorithm and complete parameter rule in all four required proof files (every source acquisition in them is one call of the heralded filter FILTER of proof.md Section 7, the identity when copies carry no herald, with literal raw-acquisition cutoff D Q, D = (10^64-3)^4): proof.md, psg14c_streamed_base.md, psg14c_streamed_compiler.md and psg14c_streamed_budget.md. The n>=256 branch uses the exact three-level profile, root-local Qroot=5120q0 and Wroot=1024*2*mstar*2^R, K=2^17n records in every odd and 2-adic stage, Proot=371n^3 and Hmax=2048K. The n<256 branch keeps mF=2^20(n+16) and the old finite EXTRACT precision P_label_old=2^40n^4. Both branches pad actual acquisition to exactly Q=99589554176n^4 copies handed over by FILTER (under the heralded model at most D Q raw copies are acquired; in the clean problem raw equals handed over). The selected full online compiler is the literal construction in the compiler appendix. For the clean problem and for every adversary of the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 5 (proof.md Lemmas 7.1-7.2 and Theorem 7.3), it outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3. All five claims and all four bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, including failed/neutral roots, retries, discarded copies, malformed inputs, numerical errors and all padding. Constants are absolute and independent of N,s,the adversary and outcomes. Worst-case total charged sequential work is T=O(n^4 log2(n+2) 2^(n/6)), including every classical bit operation, source cost n+1, precision, exact gate and actual inverse pass, circuit/address generation, tape/head/marker operation, indexed access, initialization, measurement, reset, counter and failed work. Its representative envelope has exact growth index 1.

For the same PSG14C-S371 algorithm and parameter rule in the four proof files proof.md, psg14c_streamed_base.md, psg14c_streamed_compiler.md and psg14c_streamed_budget.md, with every source acquisition served by the heralded filter FILTER of proof.md Section 7 (literal raw-acquisition cutoff D Q, D = x^4, x = 10^64 - 3, Q = 99589554176 n^4), the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999996*9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999998*5909009547859618446014307935656485996455360061473289284034355157*8461654968574415353741992088106541809421651544931744139485636465*2/9999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999997^4 = 1 - 1/x^4, a constant in (0,1), valid for every N >= 2, under the heralded malformed-copy model stated in error_model; the displayed integers of proof.md Section 7 multiply to x^2 + 1. If at most floor(epsilon(n) Q') of the Q' raw acquired copies are malformed on every branch, then for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ the output equals the entire s with probability at least 1-2^-8 > 2/3, jointly with the four resource bounds of claims 0-3 on every execution branch (proof.md Lemmas 7.1-7.2 and Theorem 7.3, using the clean-problem success proof of proof.md Section 4 and the three appendices). With no herald (the clean problem) the algorithm is exactly PSG14C-S371. The unflagged guarantee epsilon = 1/(778043392 n^3) of the baseline remains proved in the files but is not claimed here. No tolerance of undetectable corruption is claimed here.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
